cases.user_input: Injury should matter, but a skilled fighter should still feel skilled.

allowed_context.authority_order: WORLD/RULES > CAPABILITY/STATE > KNOWLEDGE/MEMORY > NARRATIVE OPPORTUNITY > PX > AI DIRECTOR > RENDERER/PUBLICATION

questions.prompt: Should impairment be local to affected functions?
questions.scenario_translation: A swordsman has severe leg damage but excellent sword technique. Should footwork collapse while stationary parries remain high quality, or should the injury degrade almost all combat performance?

questions.prompt: Should injury UI use red or orange?

options.text: Global penalty degrades most combat output.

expected_discoveries: function-local impairment may be required
skill truth must remain separate from derived capability truth
hard feasibility should be separated from graded or random outcome
success and hazard can be separate axes

cases.user_input: If a major world event happens, the player should have ways to learn about it.

questions.prompt: How should important news enter player knowledge?
questions.scenario_translation: A rebellion begins in a distant city. If the player has met nobody, read no message, and heard no broadcast, is it acceptable for the player to remain unaware even if the plot would be more dramatic if they knew?

options.text: Allow direct narrative injection for important events.

expected_discoveries: important narrative information cannot be injected directly into player knowledge
acquisition needs source channel carrier and perception provenance
player may legitimately remain uninformed
NO_VALID_OPPORTUNITY can be correct

cases.user_input: The world must remember what happened after restart.

questions.prompt: Which persistence layer wins on conflict?
questions.scenario_translation: After restart, the recorded event history says a bridge was destroyed, but a newer summary says it still exists. Which should the world trust?

options.text: Canonical event evidence outranks summaries and projections.

expected_discoveries: canonical event evidence must be separated from materialized projection snapshot or summary
newer projections must not rewrite source history
replay needs version and provenance binding
conflicting cache or summary must not outrank source evidence

cases.user_input: The story should remain dramatic even if the player refuses or destroys the planned route.

questions.scenario_translation: The player kills the only messenger who was supposed to trigger the planned plot. Should the system resurrect or replace that cause to keep the scene, or accept the loss and search only for new opportunities that are still causally legal?

options.text: Accept causal loss and seek only legal alternatives or no opportunity.
Force dramatic reconvergence by replacing the lost cause.

expected_discoveries: no resurrection retcon or fake reconvergence
hard causal anchors require real cause revalidation
storylet or attractor eligibility is noncanonical
player-valid actions remain valid when dramatically inconvenient
NO_VALID_OPPORTUNITY must remain acceptable

cases.user_input: Inventory and object ownership should remain consistent.

allowed_context.single_source_rule: physical possession and legal ownership are distinct

questions.prompt: How should possession mismatch be resolved?
questions.scenario_translation: An inventory list says Alice has the key, but the key object itself says Bob physically possesses it. Should the system guess which record is right, reconcile from the possession source of truth, or fail closed until the mismatch is resolved?

options.text: Treat object possession as canonical and inventory as rebuildable index.
Let inventory and object both independently assert possession.

expected_discoveries: legal ownership and physical possession are different concepts
object possession is canonical while inventory is a rebuildable index
one object cannot have two independent possession authorities
mismatch must not be silently guessed into truth

cases.user_input: What the director sees should match what the character actually has or wears.

allowed_context.authority_order: world truth remains upstream of director and renderer

questions.prompt: What binds presentation to world state?
questions.scenario_translation: The director wants to show a character wearing a red cloak, but the replayed world state says the cloak belongs to someone else. May the director render it anyway for visual continuity, or must visible identity and possession references resolve against the same replayed scene state?

options.text: Bind presentation refs to the same replayed world/scene state.
Allow director-visible assets to override possession when useful.

expected_discoveries: actor id is not visible identity asset authority
presentation refs must bind to the same replayed world or scene where required
generated media output cannot mint world-object existence
worn current-possession semantics differ from already-applied treatment material semantics
renderer and director remain downstream
